lines.text: You fall off a ferry in the Pacific and gasp in seawater.
lines.tts: You fall off a ferry in the Pacific and gasp in seawater.

lines.text: And you're fine.
lines.tts: And you're fine.

lines.text: No coughing. No burning. Your chest just keeps going, like you've done this forever.
lines.tts: No coughing. No burning. Your chest just keeps going, like you've done this forever.

lines.text: Something bumps your back and holds on. A remora. It thinks you're a shark.
lines.tts: Something bumps your back and holds on. A remora. It thinks you're a shark.

lines.text: Everyone up there breathes air. Everyone but you.
lines.tts: Everyone up there breathes air. Everyone but you.

lines.text: And here's the catch: air doesn't work for you anymore. You can't climb back on.
lines.tts: And here's the catch: air doesn't work for you anymore. You can't climb back on.

lines.text: Under you, the floor is 4 kilometres down. The deepest floor on Earth is a trench, a few hundred kilometres south-west of you.
lines.tts: Under you, the floor is four kilometres down. The deepest floor on Earth is a trench, a few hundred kilometres south-west of you.

lines.text: And a line on your way down is a wall.
lines.tts: And a line on your way down is a wall.

lines.text: So you go down.
lines.tts: So you go down.

lines.text: What if you could breathe underwater?
lines.tts: What if you could breathe underwater?

lines.text: One change: your body can pull oxygen out of water.
lines.tts: One change: your body can pull oxygen out of water.

lines.text: One promise: every time the ocean tries to kill you, you get the fix a real animal already uses.
lines.tts: One promise: every time the ocean tries to kill you, you get the fix a real animal already uses.

lines.text: Until there isn't one.
lines.tts: Until there isn't one.

lines.text: Everything else stays human: daylight eyes, and blood at 37 degrees.
lines.tts: Everything else stays human: daylight eyes, and blood at thirty-seven degrees.

lines.text: Keep an eye on that number. It's already moving.
lines.tts: Keep an eye on that number. It's already moving.

lines.text: First, the bad news: seawater holds about 30 times less oxygen than air.
lines.tts: First, the bad news: seawater holds about thirty times less oxygen than air.

lines.text: So about 60 litres of sea has to pour through you every minute.
lines.tts: So about sixty litres of sea has to pour through you every minute.

lines.text: A bathtub every two and a half minutes.
lines.tts: A bathtub every two and a half minutes.

lines.text: Lungs can't. Water is heavy, and lungs push it in and out the same pipe.
lines.tts: Lungs can't. Water is heavy, and lungs push it in and out the same pipe.

lines.text: In 1966, a lab mouse breathed oxygen-rich liquid and lived. Breathing out was the hard part.
lines.tts: In nineteen sixty-six, a lab mouse breathed oxygen-rich liquid and lived. Breathing out was the hard part.

lines.text: You try to shout for help. Nothing comes out. No air, no voice.
lines.tts: You try to shout for help. Nothing comes out. No air, no voice.

lines.text: The remora looks relieved.
lines.tts: The remora looks relieved.

lines.text: So here's your first fix, borrowed from every fish alive: gills.
lines.tts: So here's your first fix, borrowed from every fish alive: gills.

lines.text: Water goes in your mouth and out behind your jaw, with your blood flowing against it.
lines.tts: Water goes in your mouth and out behind your jaw, with your blood flowing against it.

lines.text: That grabs up to 80 percent of the oxygen. Your lungs managed a quarter.
lines.tts: That grabs up to eighty percent of the oxygen. Your lungs managed a quarter.

lines.text: Easy. Except breathing water does one more thing to you, and you won't feel it yet.
lines.tts: Easy. Except breathing water does one more thing to you, and you won't feel it yet.

lines.text: 200 metres. For a while, this is the best swim of your life.
lines.tts: two hundred metres. For a while, this is the best swim of your life.

lines.text: Every 10 metres adds an atmosphere of pressure, crushing the air inside divers.
lines.tts: Every ten metres adds an atmosphere of pressure, crushing the air inside divers.

lines.text: But you have no air left to crush. Water floods your sinuses and ears, and water barely squeezes.
lines.tts: But you have no air left to crush. Water floods your sinuses and ears, and water barely squeezes.

lines.text: The deepest anyone has dived on a single breath is 253 metres. You pass it without noticing.
lines.tts: The deepest anyone has dived on a single breath is two hundred and fifty-three metres. You pass it without noticing.

lines.text: Then a blue whale slides under you, longer than two buses.
lines.tts: Then a blue whale slides under you, longer than two buses.

lines.text: It doesn't even look at you. Good.
lines.tts: It doesn't even look at you. Good.

lines.text: Problem one: salt. The sea you keep swallowing is about 3 times saltier than your blood.
lines.tts: Problem one: salt. The sea you keep swallowing is about three times saltier than your blood.

lines.text: Fish have the fix: gill cells that pump salt back out. Now so do you.
lines.tts: Fish have the fix: gill cells that pump salt back out. Now so do you.

lines.text: Problem two: light. About 1 percent of the sunlight gets this deep, and your eyes were made for beaches. No fix for that.
lines.tts: Problem two: light. About one percent of the sunlight gets this deep, and your eyes were made for beaches. No fix for that.

lines.text: Your fingertips have gone white. You decide it's just the light.
lines.tts: Your fingertips have gone white. You decide it's just the light.

lines.text: 1,000 metres. The light isn't dim anymore. It's gone.
lines.tts: one thousand metres. The light isn't dim anymore. It's gone.

lines.text: Then the dark starts to sparkle: around 3 in 4 animals here make their own light.
lines.tts: Then the dark starts to sparkle: around three in four animals here make their own light.

lines.text: Problem three: something glowing drifts up to your face. An anglerfish, small enough for your palm.
lines.tts: Problem three: something glowing drifts up to your face. An anglerfish, small enough for your palm.

lines.text: But here's the thing. None of that was ever the real problem.
lines.tts: But here's the thing. None of that was ever the real problem.

lines.text: The real problem has been killing you since the ferry, and it's on screen right now.
lines.tts: The real problem has been killing you since the ferry, and it's on screen right now.

lines.text: Your blood. 37 degrees, remember? The water here is 4.
lines.tts: Your blood. thirty-seven degrees, remember? The water here is four.

lines.text: Gills swap heat too. Your blood leaves them as cold as the sea.
lines.tts: Gills swap heat too. Your blood leaves them as cold as the sea.

lines.text: At the surface, you were losing heat about 30 times faster than you make it.
lines.tts: At the surface, you were losing heat about thirty times faster than you make it.

lines.text: Here, it's a hundred. Your gills are a radiator, and the ocean is the room.
lines.tts: Here, it's a hundred. Your gills are a radiator, and the ocean is the room.

lines.text: Hypothermia starts at 35 degrees. You passed it a while ago.
lines.tts: Hypothermia starts at thirty-five degrees. You passed it a while ago.

lines.text: Down here, you've got minutes.
lines.tts: Down here, you've got minutes.

lines.text: Except a few fish cheat the cold, and their cheat is real.
lines.tts: Except a few fish cheat the cold, and their cheat is real.

lines.text: In a bluefin tuna, warm blood heading out hands its heat to cold blood coming in, through a tangle of tiny vessels.
lines.tts: In a bluefin tuna, warm blood heading out hands its heat to cold blood coming in, through a tangle of tiny vessels.

lines.text: It's your gill trick run backwards, saving heat instead of grabbing oxygen.
lines.tts: It's your gill trick run backwards, saving heat instead of grabbing oxygen.

lines.text: So your third fix: a tuna's heat exchanger, between your gills and the rest of you.
lines.tts: So your third fix: a tuna's heat exchanger, between your gills and the rest of you.

lines.text: The readout stops falling. But tuna stay warm by never stopping, and now neither can you.
lines.tts: The readout stops falling. But tuna stay warm by never stopping, and now neither can you.

lines.text: 2,000 metres. A click hits you so hard you feel it in your teeth.
lines.tts: two thousand metres. A click hits you so hard you feel it in your teeth.

lines.text: Then faster and faster, until the clicks blur into a buzz.
lines.tts: Then faster and faster, until the clicks blur into a buzz.

lines.text: That's a sperm whale. When its clicks become a buzz, it's closing in on something.
lines.tts: That's a sperm whale. When its clicks become a buzz, it's closing in on something.

lines.text: You're warm, you're moving, and you're about the size of what it eats.
lines.tts: You're warm, you're moving, and you're about the size of what it eats.

lines.text: The buzz hits you in the chest. Then the whale turns away.
lines.tts: The buzz hits you in the chest. Then the whale turns away.

lines.text: It wanted a giant squid, with eyes as wide as dinner plates. You don't make the cut.
lines.tts: It wanted a giant squid, with eyes as wide as dinner plates. You don't make the cut.

lines.text: Here's the problem nobody warned you about: every fix makes you better at the deep, and worse at everything else.
lines.tts: Here's the problem nobody warned you about: every fix makes you better at the deep, and worse at everything else.

lines.text: Many deep fish brought up to the surface don't survive the trip. You're turning into one.
lines.tts: Many deep fish brought up to the surface don't survive the trip. You're turning into one.

lines.text: 4,000 metres. You land on the floor of the Pacific: mud, cold, and 400 atmospheres.
lines.tts: four thousand metres. You land on the floor of the Pacific: mud, cold, and four hundred atmospheres.

lines.text: Your gills are fine. Your molecules are not.
lines.tts: Your gills are fine. Your molecules are not.

lines.text: Pressure this strong squeezes your proteins out of shape. Your hands shake. Your thoughts slow.
lines.tts: Pressure this strong squeezes your proteins out of shape. Your hands shake. Your thoughts slow.

lines.text: In 1992, a diver in a French chamber survived the pressure of 701 metres, a human record.
lines.tts: In nineteen ninety-two, a diver in a French chamber survived the pressure of seven hundred and one metres, a human record.

lines.text: You're almost 6 times deeper. But deep fish carry a molecule called TMAO that props proteins back into shape.
lines.tts: You're almost six times deeper. But deep fish carry a molecule called T-M-A-O that props proteins back into shape.

lines.text: Your fourth fix: you pack your cells with it. The shaking stops.
lines.tts: Your fourth fix: you pack your cells with it. The shaking stops.

lines.text: But there's a ceiling: the deeper you go, the more you need, and around 8,200 metres your cells get as concentrated as the sea.
lines.tts: But there's a ceiling: the deeper you go, the more you need, and around eight thousand two hundred metres your cells get as concentrated as the sea.

lines.text: In 2014, scientists predicted that's where fish run out. It's the wall on your route.
lines.tts: In twenty fourteen, scientists predicted that's where fish run out. It's the wall on your route.

lines.text: The trench is still days away. So you walk.
lines.tts: The trench is still days away. So you walk.
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: Then a brand-new problem: you're starving.
lines.tts: Then a brand-new problem: you're starving.
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: Staying warm burns food, and about 1 percent of what grows in sunlight ever reaches this mud.
lines.tts: Staying warm burns food, and about one percent of what grows in sunlight ever reaches this mud.
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: The remora has gone quiet.
lines.tts: The remora has gone quiet.
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: So, honestly, where could you live?
lines.tts: So, honestly, where could you live?
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: The open ocean? Nothing to eat. The abyss? You're in it.
lines.tts: The open ocean? Nothing to eat. The abyss? You're in it.
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: Unless you find a vent, a hot spring on the seafloor crowded with life.
lines.tts: Unless you find a vent, a hot spring on the seafloor crowded with life.
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: But your best home is a coral reef, 30 metres down, still in the sunshine.
lines.tts: But your best home is a coral reef, thirty metres down, still in the sunshine.
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: Except you can't go back up. Not in a body tuned for the abyss.
lines.tts: Except you can't go back up. Not in a body tuned for the abyss.
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: And then, ahead of you, the floor just ends.
lines.tts: And then, ahead of you, the floor just ends.
lines.section: L9 THE ABYSS PLAIN · LOW POINT -> TURN

lines.text: 8,200 metres. The trench walls close in.
lines.tts: eight thousand two hundred metres. The trench walls close in.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: Right at the line, a pale fish drifts past like a wet tissue. A snailfish.
lines.tts: Right at the line, a pale fish drifts past like a wet tissue. A snailfish.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: One trench north, in 2022, a camera filmed its cousin at 8,336 metres. No fish has ever been seen deeper.
lines.tts: One trench north, in twenty twenty-two, a camera filmed its cousin at eight thousand three hundred and thirty-six metres. No fish has ever been seen deeper.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: This is the wall. There's no animal left to borrow from.
lines.tts: This is the wall. There's no animal left to borrow from.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: The remora lets go and drifts back up toward the light.
lines.tts: The remora lets go and drifts back up toward the light.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: From here on, this is our guess, not known science.
lines.tts: From here on, this is our guess, not known science.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: You can stay at the line, where your body still makes sense. Or pay for the last 2,700 metres with the only thing you have left: the way back.
lines.tts: You can stay at the line, where your body still makes sense. Or pay for the last two thousand seven hundred metres with the only thing you have left: the way back.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: You keep packing your cells past the limit. They swell with sea. They hold.
lines.tts: You keep packing your cells past the limit. They swell with sea. They hold.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: And they'll never work in the shallows again.
lines.tts: And they'll never work in the shallows again.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: You go down.
lines.tts: You go down.
lines.section: L10 CLIMAX · THE LINE -> CHALLENGER DEEP

lines.text: 10,935 metres. Challenger Deep.
lines.tts: ten thousand nine hundred and thirty-five metres. Challenger Deep.

lines.text: No light. No sound. Just a puff of grey mud where you land.
lines.tts: No light. No sound. Just a puff of grey mud where you land.

lines.text: Over 1,000 atmospheres: a small car parked on each of your thumbnails.
lines.tts: Over one thousand atmospheres: a small car parked on each of your thumbnails.

lines.text: And finally, food. Amphipods, little shrimp-like scavengers, swarm over anything that sinks.
lines.tts: And finally, food. Amphipods, little shrimp-like scavengers, swarm over anything that sinks.

lines.text: Down here, you're the thing that sank.
lines.tts: Down here, you're the thing that sank.

lines.text: You eat them. They nibble you back. Fair.
lines.tts: You eat them. They nibble you back. Fair.

lines.text: In 2019, scientists opened up amphipods from this trench. Every single one had man-made fibres in its gut.
lines.tts: In twenty nineteen, scientists opened up amphipods from this trench. Every single one had man-made fibres in its gut.

lines.text: Your first meal in 6 days, and your world got to it first.
lines.tts: Your first meal in six days, and your world got to it first.

lines.text: You look up. 11 kilometres above you, the ferry is still crossing. The remora is up there somewhere.
lines.tts: You look up. eleven kilometres above you, the ferry is still crossing. The remora is up there somewhere.

lines.text: So, could you breathe underwater? Yes. That part's easy.
lines.tts: So, could you breathe underwater? Yes. That part's easy.

lines.text: You'd need gills, salt pumps, a tuna's heat exchanger and a deep fish's chemistry. And you'd pay with the way home.
lines.tts: You'd need gills, salt pumps, a tuna's heat exchanger and a deep fish's chemistry. And you'd pay with the way home.

lines.text: Getting in was never the hard part. Getting out is.
lines.tts: Getting in was never the hard part. Getting out is.

lines.text: So, back at that ferry rail: would you jump? And where would you stop: the reef, the vent, or the line?
lines.tts: So, back at that ferry rail: would you jump? And where would you stop: the reef, the vent, or the line?

lines.text: Want to see what happens when you try to swim back up? Tell me.
lines.tts: Want to see what happens when you try to swim back up? Tell me.
